introduction.title: What is an AI Engineer?
introduction.description: AI Engineers are professionals who design, develop, and deploy artificial intelligence systems. They bridge the gap between data science and software engineering, creating practical AI solutions that solve real-world problems.
responsibilityList: Design and develop machine learning models
Build scalable AI systems and infrastructure
Deploy and maintain AI models in production
Stay updated with latest AI research and technologies

reasons.title: High Demand
reasons.description: AI Engineers are among the most sought-after professionals globally, with salaries ranging from $120,000 to $300,000+

reasons.title: Innovation
reasons.description: Work on cutting-edge technology that's transforming industries from healthcare to finance to entertainment

reasons.title: Impact
reasons.description: Build solutions that can positively impact millions of lives and solve critical global challenges

reasons.title: Growth
reasons.description: Continuous learning in a rapidly evolving field with endless opportunities for professional development

roadmap.title: Your Learning Roadmap
roadmap.subtitle: Follow this comprehensive path to master AI engineering

phase1.title: Phase 1: Foundations
phase1.description: Build a strong foundation in mathematics, programming, and computer science fundamentals

topics.name: Mathematics
items: Linear Algebra: Vectors, matrices, eigenvalues, eigenvectors
Calculus: Derivatives, gradients, chain rule, optimization
Probability & Statistics: Distributions, Bayes theorem, hypothesis testing
Discrete Mathematics: Graph theory, combinatorics, logic

topics.name: Programming
items: Python: Syntax, data structures, OOP, functional programming
NumPy: Array operations, broadcasting, linear algebra
Pandas: Data manipulation, cleaning, analysis
Data Visualization: Matplotlib, Seaborn, Plotly

topics.name: Computer Science Fundamentals
items: Algorithms: Sorting, searching, dynamic programming
Data Structures: Trees, graphs, hash tables, heaps
Complexity Analysis: Big O notation, time/space complexity
Software Engineering: Version control (Git), testing, debugging

phase2.title: Phase 2: Machine Learning Basics
phase2.description: Master the fundamentals of machine learning and statistical modeling

topics.name: Supervised Learning
items: Linear Regression: Simple, multiple, polynomial regression
Logistic Regression: Binary and multiclass classification
Decision Trees: CART, pruning, ensemble methods
Random Forests: Bagging, feature importance
Support Vector Machines: Kernels, margin optimization
k-Nearest Neighbors: Distance metrics, curse of dimensionality

topics.name: Unsupervised Learning
items: K-Means Clustering: Centroid-based clustering, elbow method
Hierarchical Clustering: Dendrograms, linkage methods
DBSCAN: Density-based clustering, outlier detection
Dimensionality Reduction: PCA, t-SNE, UMAP
Association Rules: Apriori, FP-Growth algorithms

topics.name: Model Evaluation
items: Metrics: Accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, ROC-AUC
Cross-Validation: k-fold, stratified, time series split
Bias-Variance Tradeoff: Underfitting, overfitting, regularization
Hyperparameter Tuning: Grid search, random search, Bayesian optimization

phase3.title: Phase 3: Deep Learning
phase3.description: Dive deep into neural networks and modern deep learning architectures

topics.name: Neural Network Fundamentals
items: Perceptron & Multi-Layer Perceptrons
Activation Functions: ReLU, Sigmoid, Tanh, Swish
Backpropagation: Gradient descent, chain rule
Optimization: SGD, Adam, RMSprop, learning rate schedules
Regularization: Dropout, batch normalization, weight decay
Initialization: Xavier, He, transfer learning

topics.name: Convolutional Neural Networks
items: CNN Architecture: Convolution, pooling, stride, padding
Classic Models: LeNet, AlexNet, VGG, ResNet, Inception
Modern Architectures: EfficientNet, Vision Transformers
Transfer Learning: Feature extraction, fine-tuning
Object Detection: YOLO, R-CNN, SSD, RetinaNet
Image Segmentation: U-Net, Mask R-CNN, DeepLab

topics.name: Recurrent Neural Networks
items: RNN Basics: Sequential processing, hidden states
LSTM & GRU: Gates, memory cells, vanishing gradients
Bidirectional RNNs: Forward and backward processing
Sequence-to-Sequence: Encoder-decoder, attention mechanism
Time Series Forecasting: Univariate, multivariate prediction

topics.name: Transformers & Attention
items: Self-Attention Mechanism: Query, key, value
Multi-Head Attention: Parallel attention layers
Positional Encoding: Absolute, relative positions
Transformer Architecture: Encoder, decoder stacks
BERT: Pre-training, fine-tuning, masked language modeling
GPT: Autoregressive generation, prompt engineering
Vision Transformers: Patch embedding, ViT, DEIT

phase4.title: Phase 4: Specialized AI Domains
phase4.description: Explore specialized areas of AI including NLP, Computer Vision, and more

topics.name: Natural Language Processing
items: Text Preprocessing: Tokenization, lemmatization, stopwords
Word Embeddings: Word2Vec, GloVe, FastText
Contextual Embeddings: ELMo, BERT, GPT embeddings
Text Classification: Sentiment analysis, topic modeling
Named Entity Recognition: CRF, BiLSTM-CRF, Transformer-based
Machine Translation: Seq2seq, attention, transformer models
Question Answering: Extractive, abstractive, retrieval-based
Text Generation: GPT, fine-tuning, prompt engineering
Large Language Models: GPT-4, Claude, LLaMA, deployment

topics.name: Computer Vision
items: Image Processing: Filtering, edge detection, morphology
Feature Extraction: SIFT, SURF, HOG, ORB
Image Classification: CNNs, transfer learning, data augmentation
Object Detection: Two-stage (R-CNN) vs one-stage (YOLO)
Semantic Segmentation: FCN, U-Net, DeepLab, Mask R-CNN
Face Recognition: FaceNet, ArcFace, verification vs identification
Pose Estimation: OpenPose, MediaPipe, 2D and 3D pose
Video Analysis: Action recognition, tracking, temporal modeling
Generative Models: GANs, VAEs, Diffusion Models, Stable Diffusion

topics.name: Reinforcement Learning
items: RL Fundamentals: Agent, environment, reward, policy
Markov Decision Process: States, actions, transitions, rewards
Value-Based Methods: Q-Learning, DQN, Double DQN
Policy-Based Methods: Policy gradient, REINFORCE
Actor-Critic: A2C, A3C, advantage function
Advanced RL: PPO, TRPO, SAC, TD3
Multi-Agent RL: Cooperation, competition, communication
Applications: Game AI, robotics, resource optimization

phase5.title: Phase 5: MLOps & Production
phase5.description: Learn to deploy, monitor, and maintain AI systems in production environments

topics.name: Model Deployment
items: Model Serialization: Pickle, joblib, ONNX, TensorFlow SavedModel
API Development: FastAPI, Flask, REST, GraphQL
Containerization: Docker, Docker Compose, multi-stage builds
Orchestration: Kubernetes, deployments, services, ingress
Serverless: AWS Lambda, Google Cloud Functions, edge deployment
Model Serving: TensorFlow Serving, TorchServe, Triton

topics.name: MLOps Practices
items: Version Control: Git, DVC (Data Version Control), model versioning
Experiment Tracking: MLflow, Weights & Biases, Neptune
Pipeline Automation: Airflow, Kubeflow, MLflow Pipelines
CI/CD for ML: GitHub Actions, Jenkins, automated testing
Model Registry: Centralized model management, metadata tracking
Feature Stores: Feast, Tecton, feature engineering pipelines

topics.name: Monitoring & Maintenance
items: Model Monitoring: Performance metrics, data drift, concept drift
Logging: Structured logging, log aggregation, analysis
Alerting: Threshold-based, anomaly detection, PagerDuty
A/B Testing: Experimentation, statistical significance
Model Retraining: Scheduled, triggered, online learning
Performance Optimization: Quantization, pruning, distillation

topics.name: Cloud Platforms
items: AWS: SageMaker, EC2, S3, Lambda, ECS, EKS
Google Cloud: Vertex AI, Compute Engine, Cloud Storage, GKE
Azure: Machine Learning, VMs, Blob Storage, AKS
Infrastructure as Code: Terraform, CloudFormation, Pulumi

phase6.title: Phase 6: Advanced Topics
phase6.description: Stay current with cutting-edge AI research and emerging technologies

topics.name: Advanced Architectures
items: Neural Architecture Search: AutoML, DARTS, EfficientNet
Graph Neural Networks: GCN, GAT, GraphSAGE
Meta-Learning: Few-shot learning, MAML, Prototypical Networks
Self-Supervised Learning: Contrastive learning, SimCLR, MoCo
Multimodal Learning: CLIP, DALL-E, Flamingo, unified models

topics.name: Generative AI
items: Generative Adversarial Networks: StyleGAN, CycleGAN, Pix2Pix
Variational Autoencoders: VAE, β-VAE, VQ-VAE
Diffusion Models: DDPM, DDIM, Latent Diffusion, Stable Diffusion
Text-to-Image: DALL-E 2, Midjourney, Stable Diffusion
Large Language Models: GPT-4, Claude, LLaMA, prompt engineering
Retrieval-Augmented Generation: RAG, vector databases, embeddings

topics.name: AI Ethics & Safety
items: Fairness: Bias detection, mitigation strategies, fair ML
Interpretability: LIME, SHAP, attention visualization, saliency maps
Privacy: Differential privacy, federated learning, secure computation
Robustness: Adversarial examples, defense mechanisms
AI Alignment: Value alignment, safety constraints, RLHF
Responsible AI: Ethics guidelines, societal impact assessment

topics.name: Specialized Applications
items: Healthcare AI: Medical imaging, diagnosis, drug discovery
Financial AI: Algorithmic trading, fraud detection, risk assessment
Autonomous Systems: Self-driving cars, robotics, drone navigation
Recommendation Systems: Collaborative filtering, content-based, hybrid
Speech Processing: ASR, TTS, voice cloning, emotion recognition
Time Series: Forecasting, anomaly detection, causal inference

items.title: Build Projects, Not Just Tutorials
items.description: Don't just follow tutorials. Build your own projects to truly understand concepts and showcase your skills.

items.title: Read Research Papers
items.description: Stay current by reading papers from arXiv, conferences (NeurIPS, ICML, CVPR). Start with recent survey papers.

items.title: Contribute to Open Source
items.description: Contribute to ML frameworks and projects. It's great for learning and building your professional network.

items.title: Master the Fundamentals
items.description: Don't skip mathematics and classical ML. They're crucial for understanding why things work and debugging.

items.title: Practice on Real Data
items.description: Work with messy, real-world datasets. Learn to clean data, handle missing values, and deal with imbalances.

items.title: Learn to Deploy
items.description: Models are useless if they can't be deployed. Learn Docker, APIs, cloud platforms, and MLOps practices.

items.title: Join the Community
items.description: Engage with the AI community through Twitter, Discord, Reddit, and local meetups. Learn from others' experiences.

items.title: Document Your Work
items.description: Write blog posts, create tutorials, share your projects. Teaching others reinforces your own understanding.

items.title: Experiment and Iterate
items.description: Try different approaches, compare results, and learn from failures. Keep an experiment log.

items.title: Stay Humble and Curious
items.description: AI is vast and evolving. Embrace continuous learning and don't be afraid to say 'I don't know yet'.
